newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: FOCUS - Portugal's BPI pays state $900 mln for BFE.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Portugal's BPI pays state $900 mln for BFE.

text.p: Banco Portugues de Investimento (BPI) will pay the government 136 billion escudos ($900 million) for control of Banco de Fomento e Exterior (BFE) in a move that creates the country's fourth-largest banking group, Lisbon bourse said on Wednesday.
The bourse said BPI would pay 2,615 escudos ($17.3) per share for the state's 65 percent. It will then offer to buy the remaining shares at the same price.
The price was above market expectations, prompting BFE's shares to rise and BPI's to fall when they returned to trading on Wednesday after a suspension imposed last week.
The shares were suspended on August 23 just before the government announced that BPI was the only contender left in the running to take over BFE.
BFE's shares initially rose on Wednesday to a record high of 2,560 escudos ($17) from a previous 2,545, but later settled at around 2,550 escudos.
"The price seems to have found its balance but there was quite a lot of selling after the initial rise," said one share trader.
"It stands to reason that investors who bought at between 2,000 and 2,300 escudos are going to start reaping their rewards," he added.
BPI fell on the capital call and the fact the value of the bid was more than many had expected. Its shares were trading around 200 escudos down at 1,915 with traders seeing support at 1,880-1,900.
BPI said a planned 60 billion escudo ($396 million) capital increase would be sufficient to finance the acquisition.
The Finance Ministry said last week that it had opted for BPI because it felt the bank was the best placed of the three candidates to bear the increase in debt.
The sell-off is the country's second biggest privatisation following the $1 billion sale of a second stake in Portugal Telecom three months ago.
It puts the government well on its way to its target of generating $2.5 billion from privatisations this year.
The Socialist government plans to sell off 45 percent of cement group Cimpor-Cimentos de Portugal and a stake in tobacco concern Tabaqueira this year.
